newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index holds steady at 292.90.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index holds steady at 292.90.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite investable index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, was flat at 292.90 at the start of trade on Wednesday.
Latin America edged down 0.3 percent day-on-day to 531.67, Asia was up 0.4 percent at 247.93 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were down 0.3 percent at 137.93.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index BFFO, also denominated in dollars, was down 0.13 percent day-on-day at 158.79 at 0850 GMT.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was up 0.25 percent at 475.813, calculated after the close of trade on Monday.
It touched a 1996 high at 505.452 on July 4. The year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported with one day's lag at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market local currency index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, slipped 0.01 percent to 121.70 by the start of trade on Wednesday.
By region, Latin America was up 0.22 percent at 98.70, Asia rose 0.01 to 128.45 and East Europe was down 0.46 at 159.82. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
